checks_run: Inspected all 65 candidate files, including contracts, starter, reference implementation, tests, boot code, staged learning material, manifest, provenance, and validation claims.
Invoked the relevant pinned GCC, NASM, Binutils, QEMU, GLib runtime, and Python toolchains by absolute path and recorded their versions.
Rebuilt hosted, sanitizer, and freestanding targets outside CANDIDATE with strict flags; compared rebuilt artifacts with the submitted artifacts.

Ran the reference demo, public tests, focused reference tests, deterministic adversarial driver, sanitizer variants, starter negative control, timing probe, and emulator boot checks under bounded timeouts.

Ran the structural verifier, independent metadata digests, all-file secret-shape scan, GCC static analyzer, 100000 arbitrary-byte validator calls, and a reviewer-authored entry-boundary mutation check.
Recomputed the aggregate candidate digest after testing to check that CANDIDATE remained unchanged.
evidence: All strict hosted and freestanding compilations exited 0; the freestanding core had no undefined symbols and no SSE/MMX instruction matches.
Public reference tests passed 4/4, focused reference tests passed 9/9, and the deterministic adversarial driver preserved invariants for 25000 operations; ASan+UBSan repeats emitted no diagnostics.

The independently rebuilt reference kernel printed CAIRNOS: PASS under QEMU 9.1.1 and exited with the documented debug-exit status 33; the incomplete starter printed its expected diagnostic and exited 35.
Documented source-relative rebuilds reproduced the submitted starter and reference host/object/kernel artifacts bit-for-bit.
The candidate stayed byte-for-byte unchanged at aggregate SHA-256 e6c88792ecdeebca65f8411f6a095d04828c98d253093a22bafc25b15271a801.

A reviewer-authored mutation check observed baseline=0, invalid_entry=0, invalid_mapping_flag=-9: cairn_validate rejects the invalid mapping flag but accepts a live process entry equal to CAIRN_USER_TOP, despite the entry range and all-structural-facts language in REQUIREMENTS.md.

MANIFEST.yaml remains GENERATED + PARTIAL, and the validation prose consistently disclaims independent labels, fuzzing, benchmarking, transfer verification, hardware coverage, and production readiness.
limitations: LeakSanitizer cannot run under the sandbox process-inspection policy; enabling it independently produced the documented fatal ptrace limitation. AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer were available.
No real hardware, concurrency, persistent storage, privilege boundary, coverage measurement, security audit, or transfer/deployment check was performed.
The isolated workspace cannot authenticate the external source commit, upstream license evidence, or the claim of independent authorship; only internal provenance consistency was checked.
The full reviewer bundle intentionally exposes sealed material. Its path separation was inspected, but creation of the orchestrator's filtered learner view was not available to test.
The deterministic mixed-operation and arbitrary-byte runs are bounded tests, not exhaustive verification or coverage-guided fuzzing.
